model: Bank FCFE at cost of equity (engine route), net debt zero, CET1 retention on risk-weighted-asset growth, perpetual-bond distributions and NCI charged in the flow

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026E operating income, RMB m: H1 2026 actual 33,516 (interim key data, +0.75% YoY) + H2 2026E 29,590 (FY2025 H2 actual 62,558 - 33,265 = 29,293, x 1.01). FY2025 actual 62,558 (-7.6%), FY2024 67,702. Operating income = net interest income + net fee and commission income + other non-interest income (trading/investment gains, which fell 51% in FY2025).
inputs.share_count_basis: 27,464m A + H ordinary shares (weighted average = period-end, FY2025 EPS note line 10292 and H1 2026 EPS note line ~5236), unchanged since the 2023 A+H rights issue (21,269m -> 27,464m). One class with identical economic rights, so the per-share value applies to the H share. Held FLAT: no potentially dilutive securities (basic = diluted EPS), no preference shares outstanding (interim line 3746), SBC-zero. The FY2025 annual report (line 15352-15358) says the Group, newly designated a D-SIB on 13 Feb 2026, 'has actively expanded the capital replenishment channels from external sources' - a further discounted rights issue is the dilution the flat count does not model (bear-case risk, see notes).
inputs.debt_cash_note: Bank: customer deposits (RMB2.18tn at 30 Jun 2026), interbank funding and debt securities issued (RMB474bn at H1 2026, RMB513bn at FY2025) are operating funding; cash and central-bank balances are liquidity, not surplus. Net debt is zero by construction on the FCFE route and nothing is bridged after the flows.
inputs.fcf_note: last_fcf is FY2026E FCFE, not reported OCF - capex: net profit attributable to ORDINARY shareholders ~12,430 (PBT ~16,680 = H1 10,047 + H2 6,434 x 1.03, at a 26.4% margin, less income tax, NCI and perpetual-bond distributions at 25.5%) LESS equity retained to hold CET1 at 8.4% on ~3.5% RWA growth (0.035 x 0.084 x ~2,118,000 FY2025 RWA ~= 6,200) = ~6,200-6,500. Reported OCF - capex (FY2025 -21,881; H1 2026 +119,664; FY2024 -131,181) is deposit and interbank flow noise and is not used.
inputs.sbc_source: SBC-zero: no share-based payment scheme in the FY2023-FY2025 annual reports; basic = diluted EPS (RMB0.44 FY2025); ShareRepurchases 0 in FY2023-25. House and street bases coincide, band_position is degenerate (band collapsed).
inputs.fx_note: fx_rate converts CNY (model; the Bank reports in RMB) to HKD (H-share quote): CNYHKD=X 1.1724 at 2026-10-16T22:02Z, Yahoo Finance chart API. Triangulated: USDHKD=X 7.8479 / USDCNY=X 6.6768 = 1.1754 (same source, same day; 0.25% apart). The Shanghai A share (601916.SS) closed at CNY 2.97 = HKD 3.48 on 2026-10-16, a ~44% A/H premium (normal-to-wide for a smaller Chinese bank), so the dual listing is not a parity check. Per-share values are per ordinary share and apply equally to A and H.
inputs.fy0: FY2026E (year ending 2026-12-31, unreported: H1 2026 actual + H2 estimate)
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-16T08:08:14Z HKEX regular close (Friday); valuation dated Saturday 2026-10-17
inputs.cet1_anchor: Group core tier-1 ratio 8.37% on RWA RMB2,159,695m at 30 Jun 2026 (net CET1 capital 180,817; interim lines 1365-1378); 8.40% on 2,118,335m at FY2025; 8.38% on 2,065,287m at FY2024; 8.22% on 1,943,402m at FY2023 (after the rights issue); 8.05% on 1,689,148m at FY2022. Tier-1 9.55%, CAR 11.55%, leverage 4.76% at H1 2026. Regulatory CET1 floor 7.5% plus the new D-SIB surcharge (designated 13 Feb 2026; group-1 surcharge 0.25pt) = ~7.75%, so the buffer is ~0.6pt - thinner than 0998.HK's ~1.4pt. RWA growth has been throttled from 12-15% (FY2022-23) to 6.3% (FY2024), 2.6% (FY2025) and 2.0% in H1 2026 precisely to hold the ratio flat.
inputs.ordinary_equity_anchor: Equity attributable to shareholders 206,655 at 30 Jun 2026 less perpetual bonds 24,995 = ordinary equity 181,660; BVPS RMB6.61 (interim key data). At the current_price converted at fx_rate the H share trades at ~0.3x BVPS and ~4.7x FY2025 EPS.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Single CNY cost of equity 11.0% in every scenario (risk charged once, through scenario weights, not the discount rate). Built in the flows' own currency: 10-year China Government Bond ~1.8% (ASSUMPTION, not fetched; the 10Y CGB has traded ~1.6-2.0% since 2025) + beta ~1.05 x China ERP ~6.5% = ~8.6%, plus ~2.4pt for risks the index ERP does not price for an H-share minority in this joint-stock bank. That is 0.5pt above the 10.5% used for the sibling 0998.HK (China CITIC Bank, 2026-10-12), for: a CET1 buffer of ~0.6pt over the D-SIB floor versus ~1.4pt at CITIC; explicit management language about external capital replenishment; heavier wholesale funding (debt securities + interbank ~31% of liabilities); ROE 6.8% (FY2025) vs ~9.7%; trading-gain dependence (~20% of operating income, -51% in FY2025); and recurring 2025 regulatory penalties across five branches plus a PBOC fine. Hurdle for entry price is the house 15%.
inputs.lease_treatment: Bank: IFRS 16 right-of-use depreciation and lease-liability interest (lease liabilities RMB2,691m at FY2025, AR line 8326) sit inside operating expenses and so inside the pre-tax margin. lease_cost_pct_path is zero so the charge is not taken twice; nothing is deducted as debt.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, inside the 'cash_tax_rate' deduction. The margin is calibrated to PROFIT BEFORE TAX (16,129 FY2025, after credit impairment) and the deduction covers income tax (2,568; 15.9%), profit attributable to non-controlling interests (13,561 - 12,931 = 630; 3.9%) and perpetual-bond distributions (963; 6.0%). FY2025 total 25.8% = (16,129 - 11,968) / 16,129, where 11,968 is net profit attributable to ordinary shareholders (AR FY2025 EPS note, line 10290). Perpetual bonds (24,995) and NCI are therefore NOT deducted again in a bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: bank -> dcf-methods routing row 'Bank, non-bank deposit taker, thrift'. Run as FCFE at cost of equity through the component engine, the house precedent for banks (0998.HK China CITIC Bank 2026-10-12; 0939.HK, HSBC, LYG, WF, NAB.AX etc.). First valuation of this ticker; no MEMORY.md entry. Not an owner-FCF DCF: deposits are operating funding, OCF swings from -131bn to +194bn, net debt is zero by construction. ENGINE MAPPING: revenue = operating income; ebitda_margin = pre-tax margin (after credit impairment, the real cost of a bank); SBC, D&A, leases and working capital zero; cash_tax_rate = income tax + NCI + perpetual-bond distributions, so EBIT x (1 - rate) = net profit to ORDINARY shareholders; capex = equity retained to hold CET1 at the target on RWA growth (target x RWA_t - prior target x RWA_t-1, as % of revenue, from an FY2026E RWA of RMB2,200bn), so FCF = FCFE = distributable earnings. Terminal-decade RWA growth is set equal to terminal growth so the terminal FCFE is self-consistent. The 18x terminal cap does not bind (Gordon 12.1x base, 13.0x bull, 11.3x bear). KEY FINDINGS: (1) Unlike 0998.HK, the dividend is currently COVERED: ordinary profit ~12.4bn less ~6.2bn CET1 retention leaves ~6.2bn FCFE against a ~3.6bn ordinary dividend (RMB1.31/10 shares, ~30% payout) and 0.96bn perpetual coupon - but only because RWA growth has been cut to 2-3%; the business cannot both grow at its historical 10%+ and pay. (2) ROE on ordinary equity is ~6.8%, well below an 11% cost of equity, so the fair value is a fraction of book: base terminal P/B ~0.5x. The market's 0.31x prices something close to the bear case. (3) The D-SIB designation adds a capital surcharge and the bank itself flags external capital raising; a discounted rights issue (the 2023 one lifted shares 29%) is the main way the H-share holder loses value the flat-share model does not show. DRIVER EVIDENCE: FY2025 annual (NIM 1.60% vs 1.71%; cost-to-income 34.0%; NPL 1.36%; coverage 155.4% vs 178.7%; operating income -7.6%; attributable profit -14.85%; dividend RMB1.31/10 shares) and H1 2026 interim (operating income +0.75%, attributable profit +2.05%, PBT +3.6%; NIM 1.56% vs 1.69%; cost-to-income 29.2%; NPL 1.36% flat; coverage 155.9%; no interim dividend declared). Management gives no numeric FY2026 guidance (5th Five-Year Plan 2026-2030, qualitative only). Valuation date is 9.5 months into FY2026, so FY2026E is fy0 (not discounted) and the first discounted flow is FY2027; the FY2025 final dividend paid in 2026 belongs to fy0 and is not double-counted.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: terminal nominal growth for a sub-cost-of-capital Chinese joint-stock bank (China nominal GDP ~4% less continued NIM drift and capital-constrained RWA growth), bracketed by revenue 3yr CAGR 0.8% and BVPS 4yr CAGR 2.6%; base revenue path runs 2.0% -> 3.0%
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr/5yr CAGR 7.6%/9.2% vs revenue 0.8%/5.5% and EPS -7.7%/-3.7% (>30% apart). Equity growth was driven by the 2023 A+H rights issue (shares 21,269m -> 27,464m, +29%) plus retained earnings, not operating growth; BVPS was RMB6.49 at FY2022 and RMB6.48 at FY2025 - flat for three years. Equity CAGR is NOT used as the growth rate.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are null: a bank's reported FCF (OCF - capex) is deposit-flow noise. The relevant series is net profit to ordinary shareholders: 14,223 (FY2024) -> 11,968 (FY2025), -15.9%; H1 2026 +2.05%. EPS fell from 0.57 (FY2023) to 0.44 (FY2025) on rights-issue dilution plus lower profit. NIM 2.27% (FY2021) -> 1.60% (FY2025) -> 1.56% (H1 2026).

base.growth_rationale: Operating income +2.0% FY2027 then 2.5-3.0%: NIM decline narrowing (1.56% H1 2026, -13bp YoY) and bottoming ~1.5%, balance sheet growing ~5-6% (assets +6.2% in H1 2026) but loan repricing still negative, fee income recovering (H1 2026 +11.5%), trading gains normalised at the lower FY2025 level.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-tax margin after credit impairment: FY2021 27.4%, FY2022 25.9%, FY2023 27.4%, FY2024 26.0%, FY2025 25.8%, FY2026E ~26.4% (H1 30.0% vs 29.1%; H2 seasonally weaker on provisioning). Base drifts back to 28% as cost-to-income normalises from 34% (FY2025, depressed revenue) toward ~31% and credit cost holds; no NIM recovery.
base.capex_rationale: Equity retained to hold CET1 at 8.4% (current 8.37%, ~0.6pt above the D-SIB floor) on RWA growth of 3.5% for five years, then 3.0, 3.0, 2.5, 2.5, 2.5% from FY2026E RWA RMB2,200bn (FY2025 2,118bn, H1 2026 2,160bn). RWA grew 6.3% FY2024, 2.6% FY2025, 2.0% in H1 2026. Retention / revenue = g x 0.084 x prior RWA / revenue: 10.1% in FY2027 falling to 7.3%. Terminal RWA ~RMB2,985bn, CET1 capital ~RMB251bn, terminal ordinary ROE ~7%, terminal P/B ~0.5x.
base.tax_rationale: Income tax ~16% + NCI ~4% + perpetual-bond distributions (fixed RMB963m, ~5.8% of FY2026E PBT) = 25.5%, vs 25.8% actual FY2025. Held flat; the fixed coupon's share falls slightly as PBT grows (ignored, conservative).
base.terminal_note: Gordon on FY2036 FCFE at 11.0% - 2.5% = 12.1x; 18x cap does not bind. Implied terminal P/B ~0.5x on ~7% ROE, consistent with (ROE - g)/(CoE - g).
base.narrative: Steady but sub-par joint-stock bank: NIM bottoms ~1.5%, margin recovers to 28%, RWA growth held at 3-3.5% so CET1 stays at 8.4% without a raise; the ~30% payout stays covered.

bull.growth_rationale: Sector deposit repricing (~RMB8tn of high-cost deposits rolling over through 2026) reaches joint-stock banks and NIM recovers 5-10bp; wealth-management and fee income keep growing double digits; Zhejiang franchise outgrows peers.
bull.margin_rationale: Cost-to-income back to ~29% (H1 2026 level) and credit cost eases as the coverage ratio is rebuilt from earnings; 30% is the H1 2025/2026 run-rate.
bull.capex_rationale: CET1 held at 8.4% on RWA growth of 4.0% for five years then 3.5, 3.5, 3.0, 3.0, 3.0%. Terminal ordinary ROE ~8%.
bull.tax_rationale: Fixed perpetual coupon falls to ~5% of a larger PBT.
bull.terminal_note: Gordon 1.03/0.08 = 12.9x FCFE; cap does not bind.
bull.narrative: NIM turns, fees and Zhejiang SME lending grow, margin returns to 30% and the bank grows 4% a year on internally generated capital.

bear.growth_rationale: NIM keeps compressing toward 1.4% (joint-stock banks showed no margin improvement in H1 2026), trading gains fall again with bond-market volatility; revenue repeats the FY2025 decline before stabilising.
bear.margin_rationale: Credit cost rises as coverage (155.9%, only ~16pt above the 140% floor; allowance/loans 2.12% vs 2.1% floor) must be rebuilt while SME/property stress in the Yangtze delta lifts NPL formation; margin falls toward the FY2019-20 trough before partly recovering.
bear.capex_rationale: D-SIB surcharge and regulator pressure force CET1 to be rebuilt from 8.4% to 9.0% over FY2027-29 (8.6, 8.8, 9.0%) while RWA still grows 4.0, 4.0, 3.5, 3.0, 3.0, 2.5, 2.5, 2.5, 2.0, 2.0%; retention consumes most of ordinary profit for three years (FCFE ~RMB0.5-1bn, i.e. the dividend is cut or funded by a raise). The flat share count understates the damage if the rebuild is done by a discounted rights issue instead. Terminal ordinary ROE ~5%.
bear.tax_rationale: Fixed perpetual coupon against a smaller PBT.
bear.terminal_note: Gordon 1.02/0.09 = 11.3x FCFE; cap does not bind.
bear.narrative: Margin squeeze plus a forced capital rebuild: earnings fall, CET1 must climb to 9%, distributions collapse for three years and minority holders fund the state-mandated balance sheet.

scenario_narratives.base: NIM bottoms ~1.5%, pre-tax margin recovers from 26.4% to 28%, operating income grows 2-3% and RWA growth is held at 3-3.5% so CET1 stays at 8.4% without a raise. FCFE rises from ~RMB6.5bn to ~RMB10bn; terminal ROE ~7%, terminal P/B ~0.5x.
scenario_narratives.bull: Deposit repricing reaches joint-stock banks: NIM recovers 5-10bp, fees grow, cost-to-income back to ~29%, margin 30%, RWA growth 4%. FCFE ~RMB7.5bn rising to ~RMB12bn; terminal ROE ~8%.
scenario_narratives.bear: NIM toward 1.4%, credit cost up as thin coverage is rebuilt, revenue falls again; the D-SIB surcharge forces CET1 to 9.0% by FY2029, so FCFE is ~RMB1bn for three years. Dividend cut or a discounted rights issue; terminal ROE ~5%.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 40% (above 0998.HK's 35%): CET1 buffer ~0.6pt over the new D-SIB floor with management explicitly citing external capital replenishment; coverage ratio fell 23pt in FY2025 and sits near the 140% floor; FY2025 profit fell the most among joint-stock peers; trading-gain dependence and wholesale funding; recurring branch-level penalties. Bull 15%: NIM is still falling (1.56% H1 2026, -13bp YoY) and the bank is capital-constrained, capping upside. Base 45%: H1 2026 profit +2% and flat NPLs say the FY2025 drop was partly trading-gain noise.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A bank is worth the equity cash flow it can distribute after funding its own capital requirement, discounted at the cost of equity. For China Zheshang Bank that flow is net profit to ordinary shareholders (after tax, NCI and perpetual-bond coupons) less the equity retained to hold CET1 at 8.4% on growing risk-weighted assets. The bank earns ~7% on ordinary equity against an 11% cost of equity, so it is fairly worth well under book (base ~0.5x); the H share at 0.31x book and ~4.7x earnings already discounts much of the bear case, which is why the weighted value sits above the price despite a bear-heavy weighting. The dominant risk is not earnings but capital: a thin CET1 buffer plus a new D-SIB surcharge makes a dilutive raise the most likely way an H-share holder loses money. Net debt is zero by construction; deposits are operating funding.
key_risks_to_valuation: Capital: CET1 8.37% at H1 2026 vs a ~7.75% floor after the Feb 2026 D-SIB designation; management cites external capital replenishment. A discounted rights issue like 2023's (+29% shares) would dilute H-share value; the flat share count does not model it.
NIM: 2.27% (FY2021) to 1.56% (H1 2026), still falling 13bp YoY while larger peers stabilise; further LPR cuts without deposit repricing take the bear revenue path.

Credit: allowance coverage 155.9% (vs 178.7% FY2024) and allowance/loans 2.12% are both barely above the 140% / 2.1% regulatory floors, so any NPL uptick in the Zhejiang/Yangtze SME and property book flows straight into provisions.
Earnings quality: net trading/investment gains (~20% of FY2025 operating income) fell 51% in FY2025; bond-market swings move PBT by a quarter.
Governance: recurring 2025 penalties at five branches plus a PBOC fine for AML and account-management failures; new chairman approved Feb 2026.

Currency and listing: RMB flows against an HKD quote (a 10% RMB move is a 10% move in HKD value); H shares trade at a ~44% discount to the A shares; 10% dividend withholding for H-share holders is not modelled.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API (2016.HK, HKD) at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 2.11-2.69. FX CNYHKD=X, USDCNY=X, USDHKD=X and the A share 601916.SS from the same API on 2026-10-16.
data_sources.financials: 2016.HK_Metrics.csv / metrics_normalized (FY2017-FY2025, H1/Q interim through H1 2026, RMB millions) and kpis (PBT, NetProfitTotal, dividends, cash taxes). FY2025 annual report: EPS note (ordinary profit 11,968, perpetual distributions 963, line 10277-10292), capital adequacy table (lines 2190-2215), key indicators (lines 1030-1060), D-SIB designation and external capital language (lines 15350-15358), dividend RMB1.31/10 shares (line 30). H1 2026 interim: key data (lines 340-400), capital table (lines 1355-1380), EPS note (lines 5215-5236), perpetual bonds 24,995 (line 7532), no preference shares (line 3746).
data_sources.qualitative: 2016.HK_Analysis.json (2026-10-17): guidance (no numeric FY2026 targets; NIM decline narrowing; capital priority), recent developments (H1 2026 recovery, 2025 penalties, leadership change), bull/bear cases.
